name: vllm
description: A high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs
one_liner: Software that lets a company run AI chatbot models on its own computers instead of paying OpenAI or Anthropic per word generated — like owning the factory instead of renting time on someone else's.
buyer: A startup CTO whose AI product has enough usage that per-token API bills are now a top-3 cost line, or a healthcare/legal company that legally cannot send data to a third-party API.
business_use_cases: A legal-tech startup self-hosts a model with vLLM so client documents never leave their own servers, satisfying a law firm's data-residency requirement.
A high-volume customer support SaaS switches its chatbot backend to self-hosted vLLM to cut per-conversation AI costs once volume passes a breakeven point.
A batch-processing company (e.g. transcript summarization at scale) runs nightly jobs on vLLM instead of paying API rates for millions of calls.

money_ideas.idea: Offer 'private LLM hosting' as a managed service for regulated industries (legal, healthcare) billed by usage.
Consulting: audit a startup's AI cost stack and migrate their hottest-volume endpoint from a paid API to self-hosted vLLM for a fixed project fee.

steal_this: This is infrastructure plumbing, not a weekend product — the fastest real build is a cost-optimization audit script that estimates a client's break-even point between API billing and self-hosting, sold as a cheap diagnostic report.
